clue.text: Book paddle boat docked by river lodgings

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the boat word loses its final letter

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for book
a paddle is a kind of oar
a dinghy is a small boat
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A rower books a paddle boat moored beside a river near their holiday lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: BOARDING HOUSE: DINGHY loses its Y and the Ouse, a river in Yorkshire, finishes it off.
explanation.definitionFit: A boarding house is a private home letting rooms with meals, a classic form of lodgings.

clue.text: Flier heads for branch in tree

indicators.note: heads are the leading letters, so only the opening letter of each following word counts

parts.note: the first letters of these two words
the plane is a common tree in city streets

explanation.surface: A bird flies to the top of a tree and lands on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A biplane is an aircraft with two pairs of wings, so it is something that flies.

clue.text: Shocked player gripped by American fight

indicators.note: something gripped is held inside, so the player sits within the outer letters

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American
West is one of the four players at bridge
a ruck is a scuffle or brawl

explanation.surface: A sportsman is stunned when grabbed by an American in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: AWESTRUCK: bridge players are named North, South, East and West, a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Being awestruck means stunned with wonder or amazement, a strong kind of being shocked.

clue.text: Officer Chuck is easy on the eye

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, a police officer
to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: A man called Chuck, an officer, is handsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a first name, but here it is the verb meaning throw.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishy is informal British slang for physically attractive, good-looking.

clue.text: One exiled relative taking car full of ecstasy

indicators.note: a vehicle full of something holds it inside, so the drug letter goes within the car

parts.note: nan is a grandmother

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so the relative wraps around what follows

parts.note: the Polo is a Volkswagen model
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A deported family member is driving a car stuffed with drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: the drug goes into the car first, and only then does the relative wrap around the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Bonaparte was banished twice, to Elba and then to Saint Helena, a famous exile.

clue.text: Keen barbarian finally seeing tracks

parts.note: the Huns were barbarian invaders

indicators.note: finally points to the very end, so only the closing letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the last letter of this word
RY is short for railway, a set of tracks

explanation.surface: An eager savage eventually spots the trail he has been following.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungry can mean eager or avid, as in hungry for success, matching keen.

clue.text: City's cleric wearing uniform upset general

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the whole sequence is read from bottom to top

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, plus the S of the possessive
Rev is short for Reverend
someone wearing clothes is in them
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A city vicar in uniform has upset a general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer, but it is the adjective meaning widespread.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal and general both describe something applying to everyone or every case without exception.

clue.text: Wear down old monarch with verse

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A former queen wears down her listeners with poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear away gradually, as water and wind do to rock.

clue.text: Flexible part of material is so malleable

indicators.note: part of tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: A description of some fabric as pliable and easy to shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissom means supple and lithe, able to bend gracefully, so flexible fits it.

clue.text: Exercise ahead faced by some in the media

parts.note: the press is the newspaper part of the media
up as in leading, two up or ahead in a game

explanation.surface: A reporter gets ahead of the other journalists with a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: PRESS-UP: 'faced by' puts the media word in front of the word meaning ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up, called a push-up in America, is a floor exercise raising the body with the arms.

clue.text: Note about atmosphere over by island capital

parts.note: N is short for note
an air is an atmosphere or ambience
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
on cricket scorecards b means bowled by
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A memo about the weather sent from a capital city near an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' only loosely says the note concerns the atmosphere, putting N first; the rest is a string of single-letter abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya, the seat of its government.

clue.text: Half of platypuses moved in a suitable way

indicators.note: letters that are moved are put into a different order
half of a word means only its first five of ten letters are kept

parts.note: the first half of this ten-letter word

explanation.surface: Some platypuses relocated somewhere that suits them.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptly is an adverb meaning appropriately or fittingly, done in a manner that suits.

clue.text: Size of hands clasping adult book one's left

indicators.note: hands clasping something hold it between them

parts.note: L and R, left and right hands
A is the film classification abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: read as one has left, so the letter for one departs from the book

parts.note: Genesis is the first book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone holds an adult book and finds one size of print missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's left' reads as 'one has left': the letter I, for one, departs the book. Hands are L and R, left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: Largeness is the quality of being big, a measure of bulk or dimensions, so it means size.

clue.text: Paint minor entanglement of birds with cat

indicators.note: a small tangle means a slight jumbling, only a couple of letters swap places

parts.note: emus are large flightless birds
the lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A spot of paint caught up in a small tangle of birds and a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: EMULSION: only the S and L swap, which is why the tangle is called minor.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is the water-based paint commonly used on walls and ceilings in British homes.

clue.text: Tense after short son upended flower arrangement

indicators.note: after places the tense letter behind the overturned short son rather than ahead of it
in a down entry, upended means stood on its head, so these words read from the bottom up

parts.note: curt means brief or short
S is the abbreviation for son
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A short son has knocked over a tense flower arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower arrangement' looks like one phrase but splits: a flower is something that flows, a river, and 'arrangement' is the definition. The Ure is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure is the way parts are organised and put together, the same as an arrangement.

clue.text: Remains close to male perhaps on farm retreat

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
a ram is a male sheep, one example of a farm male

explanation.surface: Remains are found near a male animal on a farm that serves as a hideaway.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu religious hermitage where people withdraw for spiritual study, a retreat.

clue.text: Cold-blooded pair working with intel

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being put into action and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two ruthless spies operating on intelligence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold-blooded' suggests heartless agents, but it is the zoological sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Reptiles are ectothermic animals whose body temperature follows their surroundings, the literal sense of cold-blooded.

clue.text: Perfect plot for Spooner and Charlie

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: to hone is to perfect; its opening sound is traded for that of the next word
a bed is a garden plot; its opening sound is traded for that of the previous word

explanation.surface: An ideal storyline for Spooner and his friend Charlie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' looks like a friend's name, but a charlie is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonehead is an informal word for a stupid person, just as a charlie is a silly fool.

clue.text: Person serving nurses knockout Asian food

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close in the arms, so the first word wraps around the next

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a person serving in the army
KO is the boxing abbreviation for knockout

explanation.surface: A soldier is caring for someone knocked out, alongside some Asian food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person serving' suggests a waiter bringing food, but it is a soldier on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A pakora is a deep-fried battered vegetable fritter from Indian and South Asian cooking.

clue.text: One selling fruit stopped by centre of Dudley

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a hole, so the selected letters block the inside of the fruit

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of this six-letter name

explanation.surface: A fruit-seller's stall gets stopped in the middle of Dudley, a West Midlands town.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar is a travelling trader who goes from place to place hawking small goods to sell.

clue.text: Sweet medication in water withdrawn

indicators.note: withdrawn suggests drawn back, so the combined letters are read backwards
in tells us the medicine sits inside the water word

parts.note: a pool is a body of water
a pill is a tablet of medication

explanation.surface: A sugary medicine is pulled out of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first and the whole result is then read the other way, so the water word ends up split around the medication.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a hard sweet on a stick, a classic children's confectionery treat.

clue.text: Spy on time to see lords and ladies

parts.note: to peer is to look closely, to spy
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone keeps an eye on the clock while watching for aristocrats.
explanation.definitionFit: The peerage is the collective body of British nobles holding titles, both lords and ladies.

clue.text: Cheap writer embracing street eatery

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the first word wraps around the next

parts.note: a Biro is an inexpensive ballpoint pen
St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A hack author on a budget hugs the street café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheap writer' sounds like a poorly paid hack; it is the British brand name for a ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal restaurant serving simple food, a kind of eatery.

clue.text: Terrible setter's following court order

indicators.note: following puts the setter's contribution behind the court abbreviation instead of in front

parts.note: dire means dreadful or terrible
CT is the abbreviation for court
the setter is I, so the setter has is I've

explanation.surface: A bad crossword setter obeys a judge's ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is 'I' in crosswords, so 'setter's' is short for 'setter has', I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: A directive is an official instruction or command issued by an authority, an order.

clue.text: Brief summary rate setter countered

indicators.note: something countered is pushed back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a pacer sets the pace or rate in a race

explanation.surface: A short report says the bank's interest-rate decision was opposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rate setter' suggests a central bank, but it is the runner who sets the pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A recap is a quick restatement of the main points, a short summary.

clue.text: Most of peninsula breaking the law

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; the definition is a gerund phrase used as a noun

indicators.note: most of means not all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Crimea is a peninsula on the Black Sea

explanation.surface: Most of a peninsula is breaking international law, as with an annexation.
explanation.definitionFit: Crime is the act of committing an offence against the law, the same as lawbreaking.

clue.text: King replacing last couple of select singers

indicators.note: replacing means one item takes over the place of another

parts.note: R is Rex, Latin for king
the final two letters of the word for select, which get swapped out
choice as an adjective means select, top quality

explanation.surface: A king takes the place of the last two members of an exclusive group of singers.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is an organised group of people who sing together, a body of singers.

clue.text: Report cuckoo regularly caged by family member

indicators.note: something caged is enclosed, so it sits inside the relative

parts.note: an aunt is a relative

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A relative keeps a cuckoo in a cage and reports on it.
explanation.definitionFit: An account is a description or narrative of events, a report of what happened.

clue.text: Ran back with defrocked vicar's explicit art?

indicators.note: back means going in the opposite direction

parts.note: tore means rushed or ran

indicators.note: a defrocked priest is stripped of his robes, so the word loses its outside letters

parts.note: the word without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A disgraced priest flees after being caught with racy pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'explicit art' is a loose description rather than a dictionary synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica is literature or artwork depicting sexual themes intended to arouse, sexually explicit creative work.

clue.text: Greater number in school near new co-ed assembled

parts.note: a prep school is a private junior school

indicators.note: things assembled are put together in a fresh form

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
taken as written, hyphen dropped

explanation.surface: A mixed school nearby has a bigger roll than the others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In school' looks like a location, but 'in' just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Preponderance means superiority in quantity, the state of outnumbering or outweighing others.
